questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning of Government and Governance' refers to.
questions.a: Government is the institution or group of people that administers a state and makes rules for its citizens, while governance is the process of exercising authority, making decisions, and implementing policies for the welfare of society.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning of Government and Governance'.
questions.a: Government is the body that rules; governance is how that body exercises power and delivers services to citizens.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Meaning of Government and Governance' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Understanding Government

concepts.title: Monarchy as a Form of Government

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Monarchy as a Form of Government' refers to.
questions.a: Monarchy is a form of government in which a single ruler, usually a king or queen, holds supreme authority that is often hereditary and may be absolute or constitutional.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Monarchy as a Form of Government'.
questions.a: In a monarchy, power is concentrated in one hereditary ruler whose authority may be unlimited (absolute) or limited by a constitution (constitutional monarchy).

questions.q: Under which section is 'Monarchy as a Form of Government' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Types of Government

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Democracy and Its Core Principles' refers to.
questions.a: Democracy is a form of government in which power is held by the people, either directly or through elected representatives, based on principles of equality, freedom, participation and rule of law.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Democracy and Its Core Principles'.
questions.a: Democracy means rule by the people, where citizens elect representatives and enjoy equal political rights protected by law.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Democracy and Its Core Principles' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Types of Government

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Dictatorship and Authoritarianism' refers to.
questions.a: Dictatorship is a form of government in which a single person or a small group holds absolute power without effective constitutional limits, often acquired by force and maintained without the consent of the people.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Dictatorship and Authoritarianism'.
questions.a: In a dictatorship, power is concentrated in one ruler or group that is not accountable to the people and does not allow free elections or opposition.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Dictatorship and Authoritarianism' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Types of Government

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Parliamentary and Presidential Systems' refers to.
questions.a: A parliamentary system is a democratic government in which the executive is drawn from and accountable to the legislature, while a presidential system has a directly or indirectly elected president who is separate from the legislature.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Parliamentary and Presidential Systems'.
questions.a: In a parliamentary system the executive is part of and responsible to parliament; in a presidential system the executive and legislature are separate and independent.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Parliamentary and Presidential Systems' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Forms of Democratic Government

concepts.title: Federal and Unitary Systems of Government

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Federal and Unitary Systems of Government' refers to.
questions.a: A federal system divides power between a central national government and regional state governments by a constitution, while a unitary system concentrates all power in a single central government.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Federal and Unitary Systems of Government'.
questions.a: Federalism shares power between central and regional governments; a unitary system keeps all power at the centre.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Federal and Unitary Systems of Government' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Distribution of Power

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Republic and Constitutional Monarchy' refers to.
questions.a: A republic is a form of government in which the head of state is an elected person and not a hereditary monarch, while a constitutional monarchy retains a hereditary monarch as ceremonial head with real power held by elected representatives.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Republic and Constitutional Monarchy'.
questions.a: In a republic the head of state is elected; in a constitutional monarchy a hereditary monarch is a ceremonial head while elected representatives govern.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Republic and Constitutional Monarchy' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Types of Government

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Evolution of Government Types' refers to.
questions.a: The evolution of government types traces the change from early tribal councils and monarchies to modern democracies and republics, driven by struggles for equality, rights and people's participation in decision-making.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Evolution of Government Types'.
questions.a: Forms of government have evolved over time from hereditary monarchies toward democratic systems based on the consent and participation of citizens.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Evolution of Government Types' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Historical Development

concepts.title: Comparison of Democratic and Non-Democratic Systems

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Comparison of Democratic and Non-Democratic Systems' refers to.
questions.a: A democratic system allows people to elect their rulers, enjoy fundamental rights and hold the government accountable, while a non-democratic system concentrates power in one ruler or group without free elections or accountability to citizens.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Comparison of Democratic and Non-Democratic Systems'.
questions.a: Democracy is based on consent, rights and accountability; non-democratic systems rest on force, lack of freedom and no accountability to the people.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Comparison of Democratic and Non-Democratic Systems' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Comparing Government Types
